metadata.title: Combining Statistical and Machine Learning Methods to Identify Predictors of Brazilian Students’ Proficiency in PISA 2018

design_fields.q1_rationale: The study does not use plausible values as the dependent variables are dichotomized proficiency categories rather than PV-based continuous achievement scores.
design_fields.q2_rationale: The matching, text-readable full PDF does not report use or explicit non-use of sampling weights; full-text search found no weight terminology. Original extraction rationale: The study explicitly states that it did not apply any student/sampling weights in the analysis.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study adjusted multilevel logistic regression analyses, which accounts for school clustering.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study mentions using internal validation methods such as random forest analysis and does not report any validation on external datasets.

design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): “The population of this study were 15-year-old students and schools from Brazil participating in PISA 2018.” “Using random forest analysis… I then adjusted multilevel logistic regression analyses…”
